With the classic JSX transform, `<App />` compiles to `React.createElement(App)`. If the file does not import `React`, that line throws `ReferenceError: React is not defined` when it runs.

If the file has a `@jsx` comment, or your ESLint config sets `settings.react.pragma`, the rule looks for that name instead of `React`.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
export function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import React from "react";

export function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}
```

{/* good */}
```jsx
/** @jsx h */
import { h } from "preact";

export function App() {
  return <h1>Hello</h1>;
}
```

## When not to use it

Turn it off if you use the automatic JSX transform (`"jsx": "react-jsx"` in `tsconfig.json`), which is what Bun does by default. That transform imports what it needs by itself, so `React` does not have to be in scope.
